govdocs-archive_org-TowardsAPsychocivili: José M. R. Delgado’s Physical Control of the Mind: Toward a Psychocivilized Society — this archive.org file — reports his brain-stimulation work. The Yale researcher’s trials raised a storm. Its meaning still stings. The book is a landmark of brain-lore and its rows.
govdocs-archive_org-VictorThornShipWitho: Victor Thorn and Mark Glenn’s Ship Without a Country: Eyewitness Accounts of the Attack on the USS Liberty gathers first-hand tales. The 1967 incident remains hotly disputed. Survivors tell their own story here. Thirty-four Americans died. The book fits the hot-history shelf.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FundForInformat: Harold Weisberg’s affidavit is a sworn court statement. Weisberg swore to his findings under oath. Affidavits carry legal weight. The affidavit endures. His word was his bond. The file belongs to the legal archive. The item is a fragment of the legal record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-ParrotBetty_Par: This statement on Betty Parrot — March 31, 1967, creator unknown — is a witness file. Witnesses shape the case. Her words count. The statement endures. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
psmith-in-the-city: Wodehouse's inimitable Psmith — monocle, charm, and effortless superiority — takes a job in a London bank, dragging his friend Mike along. Office drudgery meets Psmith's genius for elegant evasion in this early comic gem. The master's dialogue sparkles, and Psmith remains one of fiction's most delightful creations.
the-prince-and-betty: Wodehouse's comedy pairs a penniless prince with Betty, an American heiress, in a tangle of romance and mistaken identity. Set partly in New York, it shows the young master already wielding his light, sure touch. Charming early Wodehouse, full of sparkle and good humor.
sidelights-on-relativity: Albert Einstein himself explains relativity's sidelights — the ideas around his great theory — in these accessible lectures. The master popularizes his own revolution. Essential for all who wonder what it all means. Time, space, and light bend to his plain and playful explanations.
the-jewel-city: Ben Macomber celebrates the Jewel City — San Francisco's Panama-Pacific Exposition of 1915, a wonderland of palaces and lights. His account preserves the fair's magic. A glittering souvenir of a golden moment. Tower of Jewels and Palace of Fine Arts shine in his enthusiastic record.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-administrator: A 1913 entry on the administrator of church property — the steward of the Church's goods. John Creagh sets out his duties. Honesty and care are his twin laws. The entry guides bishops and pastors. Temporal goods, spiritually kept. Inventories and audits guard his stewardship.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-altar-cavity: This 1913 reference article on the altar cavity — the sepulchre for relics in the stone. Augustin Schulte describes its sealing. Martyrs' bones rest beneath the mensa. Every altar holds its saints. The tomb within the table. Its leaden box keeps the relics dry.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-amovibility: A 1913 entry on amovibility — the removable priest's tenure in canon law. William Fanning states the rules. Bishops may move their clergy at need. The mission's good comes first. A practical point of church law. Its practice serves the mission lands.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolic-maj: A 1913 entry on Apostolic Majesty — the Hungarian king's proud title. Antal Aldásy traces its papal grant. St. Stephen's crown earned the style. The Habsburgs bore it last. A title of the Danube's kings. Its style graced the imperial decrees.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-apostolicity: A 1913 entry on apostolicity — the mark of the true Church. Thomas O'Reilly proves the Catholic claim. The Church descends from the apostles. No other body bears the sign. The note of the genuine Church. Its proof is the history's verdict.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archconfrater: A 1913 entry on the archconfraternity — the head confraternity of its kind. Francis Donnelly explains its privileged rank. Rome grants it powers to affiliate. The lesser sodalities share its graces. The motherhouse of the pious unions. Its diploma hangs in many homes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-aseity: This 1913 reference article on aseity — God's existence from Himself alone. George Sauvage explains the high doctrine. No cause stands behind the First. The schools built on this rock. The metaphysics of the divine being. Its truth underlies the proofs of God.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-augustin-bonn: This 1913 reference article on Augustin Bonnetty — the editor of the Annales de philosophie chrétienne. Charles Dubray honors his long editorship. His review wedded faith and science. The Catholic press knew his zeal. A journalist of the Christian idea. His review ran for sixty years.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-baker-city: A 1913 entry on Baker City — the Oregon diocese of the high desert. Thomas Meehan gives its pioneer story. Its bishops serve the ranching towns. The Blue Mountains guard its see. A bishopric of the eastern plains. Its cathedral crowns the Powder valley.
